title: Performance canary: adaptive auto-detection & rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: The existing performance canary pipeline relied on fixed thresholds and simple windowing which produced noisy rollbacks and missed slow regressions. This change implements an adaptive auto-detection approach that uses rolling baselines, percentile-based detection, KV-cache hysteresis to avoid flapping, and a policy-driven rollout guard that can block or throttle traffic when regressions are detected. Summary of changes: detector service + API, metrics signal processor with p50/p95/p99 histograms, adaptive threshold estimator, KV hysteresis controller, rollout guard policy engine, console flags and observability hooks, e2e/perf tests and docs. Checklist: - Implement detector service (done) - Integrate detector with canary controller (done) - Add hysteresis and cooldown logic (done) - Add console UI + feature flag (done) - Add e2e and unit tests (done) - Add docs and release notes (done). Testing: unit and integration tests cover detector logic and hysteresis; e2e perf tests run against canary lab with synthetic load patterns (steady, spike, slow drift) and validated no false-positive blocks for non-regressions. Rollout plan: feature gated by default; dark launch for 24h on internal traffic, then enable on 10% customer traffic for 6h, observe, increase to 50% then 100%. Backout: canary controller can be disabled via feature flag or policy if noisy. Related work: ENG-1289 (adaptive detector design), ENG-1303 (canary controller integration). Impact: reduces noisy rollbacks and improves detection of slow regressions; initial default thresholds are conservative and adjustable per-team. No breaking changes.

release_notes: Added adaptive auto-detection for performance canaries with rollout guards and KV-hysteresis to reduce noisy rollbacks. Feature is feature-gated and defaults to conservative thresholds. Teams can configure thresholds via helm values or console. Includes new detector service, metrics processor, and e2e perf tests.
